newsitem.title: CHINA: China to decide Taiwan-China sailing by end-month.
newsitem.headline: China to decide Taiwan-China sailing by end-month.

text.p: China expects to decide by the end of the month when it will allow the first ship in 48 years to sail directly across the Taiwan strait from the Chinese mainland, an official said on Wednesday.

"The date for the first ship to cross the Taiwan strait has not yet been decided, but it is likely to be known by the end of this month," an official of the Taiwan Affairs Office of the Ministry of Communications said.
He declined to give further details, but said ministry officials were considering applications from about a dozen Taiwan shipping companies for approval to ply direct routes.
"We have no information about when we will be able to sail across the Taiwan strait," said an official of the Fujian Xiamen Shipping Co based in the southern port of Xiamen that faces Taiwan.

"The report that a Chinese ship will sail to Taiwan on Thursday is a rumour," he said by telephone, adding that the company had purchased the vessel Sheng Da recently, expressly to engage in cross-strait shipping.

Taipei's China Times on Wednesday quoted mainland sources as saying the Sheng Da, owned by China's Fujian Provincial Shipping Co but registered in Saint Vincent, would leave Xiamen for Taiwan's southern Kaohsiung port on Thursday.

The Sheng Da is one of four ships from four mainland sea freight firms approved by Taiwan on April 11 to sail directly into Kaohsiung from the mainland in an easing of a ban on direct links dating to the civil war that split them in 1949.

Nationalist-ruled Taiwan denies that the long-forbidden crossings are direct links because mainland cargoes will not be allowed to enter Taiwan customs. Rather, they can only be processed at what Taiwan is calling an "offshore transshipment centre" for onward passage to third countries.
Taiwan cargoes at Kaohsiung cannot be put aboard ships planning to cross directly to two mainland ports approved for the scheme -- Xiamen and the Fujian capital of Fuzhou.
The four approved mainland shippers are Fujian Foreign Trade Centre Shipping Co, Fujian Provincial Shipping Co, Fujian Xiamen Shipping Co and Shamen Ocean Shipping Co.
Taiwan still bans all direct contacts with the rival mainland, but faces huge pressure from Taiwan business circles to relax the ban.
Some 30,000 Taiwan firms have poured US$30 billion into mainland investments, and they say direct air, maritime and other links could trim needless costs of cultivating their China businesses.
